Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On news.ntv.co.jp the reporter circled Google's "preferred source" promotion banner (Google G logo, 「Google検索で」/「日テレNEWS NNNを優先表示」) between the article's last-update line and 関連トピック; it is one visible div.preferred-source baked into the served HTML. The repository already hides this widget with a shared multi-domain rule, so news.ntv.co.jp belongs in it, and the experiment verified the banner gone with the page intact. ## Rule `news.ntv.co.jp##.preferred-source` ## Policy rationale The complaint is an in-page promotional/annoyance widget (Google preferred-source badge) — not the site's own advertising creative, not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall and not a scam page — so none of the run instruction's closing rules applies. The repository already maintains a shared multi-domain cosmetic rule hiding exactly this `.preferred-source` widget, so the fix follows the maintainer rule 'Shared rules:⁠ extend them' and the contributing guide's placement rule (add the domain at the beginning of the cosmetic domain list). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c8f09d1582ea403dd6ab167fcb78fb862a9b0dd2/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt) By adding the domain to the existing rule on [line 1178](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/c8f09d1582ea403dd6ab167fcb78fb862a9b0dd2/AnnoyancesFilter/Popups/sections/subscriptions_specific.txt#L1178). ## Screenshots

The filter policy leaves this report to a maintainer

## Reproduced symptom

The reported anti-adblock wall on www⁠.baseball-reference.com did not appear in 15 loads of the reported player page (full-page vision:⁠ absent, no obstruction), and the captured requests contain no detector script — the detection client is an inline script in the served HTML, with the only external requests being gtm.js and config-factory JSON that existing rules already block. The run instruction only allows a rule for a non-German anti-adblock wall once captured requests show the detector script, so this goes to a maintainer instead of a filter change.

## Policy rationale

Run instruction, Filter policy:⁠ "Any other anti-adblock wall:⁠ write a rule only once the page's requests the agent captured show the detector script; without it, hand the report to a maintainer." The locked AdGuard CLI session's HAR (artifact:⁠har:⁠d1301359-a121-432a-a372-0c6e1f2606eb, 18 recorded loads) contains no anti-adblock detector script request:⁠ only www⁠.baseball-reference.com documents/assets, cdn.ssref.net assets including /req/202610281/js/br/sr-min.js, the already-redirected https:⁠//www⁠.googletagmanager.com/gtm.js?id=GTM-MC36NL2 and the already-blocked https:⁠//config.config-factory.com/baseball-reference.json fetch. The ad-block detection/recovery client that draws the reporter's modal is a \~27 KB inline <⁠script⁠> in the served HTML (status strings not detected/detected/recovered, accountId, siteId, userId, hasFsBranding, disableInstructions) rendering into the site's own popup shell #⁠modal-overlay ⁠> #⁠modal-container ⁠> #⁠modal-content; an inline script is not a request, so no loadable resource was identified that a network rule could stop. The German anti-adblock-wall rule does not apply:⁠ the page is an English-language site and the reported content is "Looks like your ad blocker is on. … Please support our site by disabling your ad blocker." The reporter screenshot's modal also offers a "Continue without supporting us" link, which the served filter policy lists among the criteria under which detection messages are not blocked; whether that alternative actually lets the user proceed is unverified and rests with the maintainer.

Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — On mobile speedtest.net a full-viewport "Speedtest is better with the app." MUI dialog covers the speed-test area; the repository's existing speedtest app-dialog rules do not match it because its links use the Speedtest Android intent:⁠// scheme. A domain-scoped element-hiding rule on that dialog passed the bound A/B/C experiment (popup gone, page integrity intact, no remaining instances). ## Rule `speedtest.net##.MuiDialog-root:has(a[href^="intent:///test#Intent;scheme=speedtest;package=org.zwanoo.android.speedtest"])` ## Policy rationale The reported defect is the site's own app-install promo popup:⁠ the AdGuard Mobile App Banners filter's stated purpose and the repository's existing speedtest.net app-dialog and self-promo rules already cover this annoyance class on this domain, so it is not the site's own advertising that policy protects. No policy rule closes the report:⁠ it is not a paywall, not a German anti-adblock wall, and not an anti-adblock wall at all (no detector request or anti-adblock overlay observed; the dialog is rendered by the page's own JS bundle). ## Place in the list [AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/74e7131dfa0d7c57081a0ebe1e44996ed38c2891/AnnoyancesFilter/MobileApp/sections/mobile-app_specific.txt) At the end of the file. ## Screenshots
